property_summary: Because withdrawReward zeroes rewardsForA before transferring, once a bonus has been paid a second withdrawReward sends 0 wei and always succeeds; the mutant keeps the reward so the second transfer of 100 wei reverts when the contract balance is exhausted.

After a successful getFirstWithdrawalBonus(r), the reward has been fully paid out, so a follow-up withdrawReward(r) sends 0 wei, still succeeds, and leaves address(c).balance unchanged; the mutant leaves the 100-wei reward un-zeroed, so the follow-up withdraw reverts (insufficient contract balance) or over-pays.

For any funded recipient, after getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) succeeds, a follow-up withdrawReward(recipient) must still succeed (it sends 0 wei because the reward was zeroed); the mutant keeps the 100-wei reward pending, so the follow-up withdraw reverts for insufficient balance.

After the first-withdrawal-bonus flow completes, a repeated withdrawReward(recipient) must pay out nothing more (rewardsForA is zeroed), so address(c).balance drops by exactly 100 wei; the mutant never clears rewardsForA and pays 100 twice, dropping 200 wei.

After a bonus withdrawal has paid out a recipient's rewards, rewardsForA[recipient] is zero, so a further withdrawReward(recipient) must pay nothing and leave address(c).balance unchanged; the mutant leaves the reward uncleared and pays 100 wei again, reducing c's balance.

After a recipient's first-withdrawal bonus has been paid out, rewardsForA is zeroed, so any further withdrawReward(recipient) pays nothing and address(c).balance is unchanged; the mutant leaves the reward uncleared and drains 100 wei again, so the test deals the contract Ether (otherwise the external call reverts and the rule holds vacuously) and asserts the balance is unchanged, which the mutant breaks.

For any admissible funding, a re-entrant recipient calling back into withdrawReward can never complete the outer withdrawReward call (the lock must make the reentrant attempt revert); the mutant, which never sets the lock, lets the reentrant path succeed so the outer call completes.

For every admissible input, withdrawReward can be called repeatedly and each call succeeds (the reentrancy lock is always released); the buggy mutant keeps the lock set forever, so a second withdrawReward call reverts.
p_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address): withdrawReward must be reusable: lock is released after each call
m_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address): withdrawReward must be reusable: lock is released after each call
